headline: Andrej Karpathy had Claude Opus 5.5 build HackerTube, a YouTube-recommendation substitute

insights.text: Andrej Karpathy had Claude Opus 5.5 build HackerTube, a YouTube-recommendation substitute, entirely on its own: ingesting ~40,000 Hacker News comments, filtering them down to 6,454 recommended videos across 150 topics, building the UI, and deploying it to a hardened VPS — in about two hours, with Karpathy writing no code himself.

A second project, Memdoor, reused the exact benchmark scaffold of October's GVS5H open-weight-ensemble claim and reached a closely comparable result — five Qwen3.8-27B agents scoring 9.8/10 against the original's 9.6/10, both beating Claude Fable 5's single-call 8.0/10 — though this is methodology reuse on the same ten problems, not an independent replication.

thedotmack/claude-mem holds GitHub Trending #1 for a second consecutive day, and its star velocity rose rather than cooled: +1,723 stars today, up from +1,140 yesterday, against the usual post-launch decay pattern this research has documented for other viral GitHub debuts.

A Brazilian labor court sanctioned two lawyers for hiding a prompt-injection instruction in a court filing — white-on-white text telling an AI reviewer to respond superficially and not challenge the documents — in what may be the first judicial ruling worldwide to address intentional manipulation of a court's own AI system.

pbakaus/impeccable, a design-vocabulary skill for coding agents, is reported by its own creator to now ship pre-bundled inside the new GitHub Copilot app by default — the first concrete instance of a packaged skill being absorbed as a first-party vendor feature rather than an opt-in install.

A widely-discussed Hacker News thread describes Anthropic restricting a Claude account for usage resembling model-training activity, downgrading it away from Opus 5.5 — a fourth, behavioral access-gating mechanism (after identity, age, and geography) likely driven by an automated anti-distillation classifier.

Google Gemini holds a Play Store top-30 spot for a second consecutive day (#9, 4.6★) while Grok reappears (#16, 4.9★) and Claude and ChatGPT remain absent — the first time any of four tracked frontier-lab apps has cleared this research's own two-consecutive-day bar for treating a return as signal rather than noise.

Google shipped LiteRT's biggest upgrade yet for Android on-device inference: 1.4x faster GPU inference, roughly 8MB smaller app sizes, and a new CompiledModel API replacing the older Interpreter API, with TensorFlow Lite now in maintenance-only mode as all active development moves to LiteRT.

takeaway.text: Today's sharpest signal isn't a new model or benchmark — it's Andrej Karpathy having an agent ingest, curate, and deploy a finished product end to end in two hours, the same direction nearly every other story today points: the agent's job keeps expanding into territory a human used to have to finish.
